newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: North says Australian gold sales too fast.
newsitem.headline: North says Australian gold sales too fast.

text.p: Diversified mining house North Ltd said on Wednesday Australia's central bank would have caused less disruption to the gold price if it had taken more time to dispose of two-thirds of its gold reserves on world markets.
"I would have liked to have seen the sales occur over a longer period of time," North's deputy managing director Malcolm Broomhead said.
"In other words, sell it in a way that it wouldn't have impacted the market the way it did," he told reporters.

The Reserve Bank of Australia's selling of 167 tonnes of gold over the last six month was a key factor behind world gold prices sinking to 12 year lows of around US$313 an ounce earlier this month, Broomhead said.
Broomhead said North's gold hedge book is currently worth about A$60 million.
About 50 percent of forecast gold production over the next five years is hedged at an average of A$645 an ounce, he said.
"We're reasonably well insulated there," he said.
However, Broomhead said there was nonetheless concern over the gold price.
"If the gold price stays where it is we will see a very big shakeout," he said.
He said exploration by gold miners worldwide was likely to suffer and that more gold mines would be targets of predators.
A "changed view by central banks" over their need to hold gold had led to concern among miners that there will be a wave of undisciplined central bank selling, sinking the price, Broomhead said.
"In other words, that there will be no coordination among central banks and they will try to offload their gold holdings," he said.
Central banks hold about 10 years worth of mine production in reserve, analysts estimate.
A more politically stable world environment and low inflation has diminished gold's image among the banks, Broomhead added.
North owns 50 percent of the Kanowna Bell and 33.33 percent of the Peak Hill gold mines in Western Australia, which produced a combined 110,000 ounces of gold for North in 1995/96.
It also has proposed developing the Lake Cowal gold mine in the eastern Australian state of New South Wales.
